captions.instagram:
How is an idli made?

Rice, urad dal, water and salt go into a vessel at night, and by morning the batter has doubled, with no yeast and no starter. Meet the wild bacteria that sour it and blow the bubbles, run your own batch on a warm night and a cold one, then watch steam set the foam into a sponge.

→ An idli is just rice, urad dal, water and salt. Cut it open and about half of it is gas cells.
→ In a wet grinder the drum turns and two granite stones roll in place, crushing soaked grain between stone and stone.
→ Urad dal is ground smooth and fluffy with air. Rice is left a little gritty, like rava.
→ No starter is added. Bacteria from the dal turn sugar into lactic acid and carbon dioxide, and urad's gum traps the bubbles.
→ On a warm night the batter doubles in 10 to 12 hours while its pH falls from about 6 to about 4.5.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/idliclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is an idli made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Rice, urad dal, water and salt go into a vessel at night, and by morning the batter has doubled, with no yeast and no starter. Meet the wild bacteria that sour it and blow the bubbles, run your own batch on a warm night and a cold one, then watch steam set the foam into a sponge.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/idliclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/idliclear

In this video:
• Two grains and a lot of air. An idli is rice and urad dal, usually two to four parts of rice for one of dal, with water and salt.
• Stone on stone. The grains are soaked for four to six hours and ground wet.
• Nobody adds a starter. The bacteria arrive on the grain.
• Warmth and time decide the rise. At 25 to 35 °C the batter roughly doubles in 8 to 14 hours while its pH falls from about 6 to about 4.5.
• Ten minutes in steam. Steam at 100 °C condenses on the cool batter and releases 2,257 kilojoules per kilogram.
• One idea, many idlis. Pour the batter on a plate and it is thatte idli.
